passages.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, To all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Timothy write this letter.
Paul and Timothy serve Christ Jesus.
They write to all the saints in Christ Jesus.
These saints live in Philippi.
The overseers and deacons are with them.
Paul and Timothy greet them.
They wish grace for them.
They wish peace for them.
Grace and peace come from God our Father.
Grace and peace come from the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Παῦλος καὶ Τιμόθεος δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ Πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Φιλίπποις σὺν ἐπισκόποις καὶ διακόνοις Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: I thank my God every time I remember you.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter.
Paul was a servant of Christ Jesus.
Paul wrote to the believers in Philippi.
Paul thanked his God.
Paul thanked God every time he remembered the believers in Philippi.
passages.original: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ μου ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ μνείᾳ ὑμῶν

passages.text: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy, because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now, being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Timothy are servants of Christ Jesus.
They write to all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi.
They include the overseers and deacons.
Paul prays for all the believers in Philippi.
He prays for them every time.
He prays for them with joy.
He feels joy because they have partnered with him in the gospel.
They have partnered with him from the first day until now.
Paul is confident about something.
God began a good work in the believers at Philippi.
God will continue this good work.
God will complete this work until the day of Christ Jesus.
passages.original: πάντοτε ἐν πάσῃ δεήσει μου ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς τὴν δέησιν ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης ἡμέρας ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν πεποιθὼς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὅτι ὁ ἐναρξάμενος ἐν ὑμῖν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτελέσει ἄχρι ἡμέρας Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, since I have you in my heart. For in my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all partners in grace with me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
Paul feels a deep affection for all of them.
Paul says it is right for him to feel this way about them.
Paul keeps them in his heart.
Paul is in chains.
Paul defends the gospel.
Paul confirms the gospel.
The believers share in God’s grace with Paul.
They are partners with Paul in grace.
They share with Paul both when he is in prison and when he defends the gospel.
passages.original: Καθώς ἐστιν δίκαιον ἐμοὶ τοῦτο φρονεῖν ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν διὰ τὸ ἔχειν με ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμᾶς ἔν τε τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀπολογίᾳ καὶ βεβαιώσει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου συνκοινωνούς μου τῆς χάριτος πάντας ὑμᾶς ὄντας

passages.text: God is my witness how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon: God is my witness.\r\nI long for all of you.\r\nI long for you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
passages.original: μάρτυς γάρ μου ὁ Θεός ὡς ἐπιποθῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ἐν σπλάγχνοις Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight, so that you may be able to test and prove what is best and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ, filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is praying for the believers in Philippi.
He wants their love to grow more and more.
He wants their love to increase in knowledge.
He wants their love to increase in all understanding.
He prays this so they can recognize what is best.
He wants them to choose what is excellent.
He wants them to be pure for the day of Christ.
He wants them to be blameless for the day of Christ.
He wants them to be filled with the fruit of righteousness.
This righteousness comes through Jesus Christ.
He wants all this to bring glory to God.
He wants all this to bring praise to God.
passages.original: Καὶ τοῦτο προσεύχομαι ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ὑμῶν ἔτι μᾶλλον καὶ μᾶλλον περισσεύῃ ἐν ἐπιγνώσει καὶ πάσῃ αἰσθήσει εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τὰ διαφέροντα ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ πεπληρωμένοι καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς δόξαν καὶ ἔπαινον Θεοῦ

passages.text: Now I want you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have actually served to advance the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Philippi.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul wants them to know something important.
Paul is in difficult circumstances.
Paul’s circumstances have helped the gospel.
Paul’s situation has actually advanced the gospel.
passages.original: Γινώσκειν δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι ἀδελφοί ὅτι τὰ κατ’ ἐμὲ μᾶλλον εἰς προκοπὴν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐλήλυθεν

passages.text: As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul is in prison.
Paul is in chains because of Christ.
Everyone in the whole palace guard knows this.
All the other people also know this.
It is clear to them that Paul is in chains for Christ.
passages.original: ὥστε τοὺς δεσμούς μου φανεροὺς ἐν Χριστῷ γενέσθαι ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ πραιτωρίῳ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν

passages.text: And most of the brothers, confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare more greatly to speak the word without fear.
passages.sermon:
Most of the brothers believe in the Lord.
They see that I am in chains for Christ.
Because of this, they have become more confident.
They now speak the word of God more boldly.
They do not feel afraid.
passages.original: καὶ τοὺς πλείονας τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἐν Κυρίῳ πεποιθότας τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου περισσοτέρως τολμᾶν ἀφόβως τὸν λόγον λαλεῖν

passages.text: It is true that some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.
passages.sermon:
Some people preach Christ.
They do this because of envy and rivalry.
Other people preach Christ.
They do this out of goodwill.
passages.original: Τινὲς μὲν καὶ διὰ φθόνον καὶ ἔριν τινὲς δὲ καὶ δι’ εὐδοκίαν τὸν Χριστὸν κηρύσσουσιν

passages.text: The latter do so in love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.
passages.sermon: Some people preach Christ.\r\nThey do this out of love.\r\nThey know I am appointed to defend the gospel.
passages.original: οἱ μὲν ἐξ ἀγάπης εἰδότες ὅτι εἰς ἀπολογίαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου κεῖμαι

passages.text: The former, however, preach Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing that they can add to the distress of my chains.
passages.sermon:
Some people preach Christ.
They do this out of selfish ambition.
They do not act with pure motives.
They think they can increase my suffering.
I am in chains.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας τὸν Χριστὸν καταγγέλλουσιν οὐχ ἁγνῶς οἰόμενοι θλῖψιν ἐγείρειν τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου

passages.text: What then is the issue? Just this: that in every way, whether by false motives or true, Christ is preached. And in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice, because I know that through your prayers and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, my distress will turn out for my deliverance.
passages.sermon:
Paul is in prison for defending the gospel.
\r\nSome people preach Christ with good motives.
\r\nOthers preach Christ with selfish motives.
\r\nPaul asks, "What is the result?"
\r\nThe result is this.
\r\nIn every way, Christ is preached.
\r\nSome preach Christ with false motives.
\r\nSome preach Christ with true motives.
\r\nPaul rejoices that Christ is preached.
\r\nPaul will continue to rejoice.
\r\nPaul knows something important.
\r\nHe knows that his situation will lead to his deliverance.
\r\nThis will happen through the prayers of the believers.
\r\nThis will also happen through the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Τί γάρ πλὴν ὅτι παντὶ τρόπῳ εἴτε προφάσει εἴτε ἀληθείᾳ Χριστὸς καταγγέλλεται καὶ ἐν τούτῳ χαίρω ἀλλὰ καὶ χαρήσομαι οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν δεήσεως καὶ ἐπιχορηγίας τοῦ Πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed, but will have complete boldness so that now as always Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul is in prison for preaching Christ.
Paul expects and hopes for something.
Paul expects that he will not be ashamed.
Paul hopes that he will not be ashamed.
Paul expects to have complete boldness.
Paul hopes to have complete boldness.
Paul wants to be bold now, just as he has always been.
Paul wants Christ to be exalted in his body.
Paul wants Christ to be exalted whether he lives or dies.
passages.original: κατὰ τὴν ἀποκαραδοκίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα μου ὅτι ἐν οὐδενὶ αἰσχυνθήσομαι ἀλλ’ ἐν πάσῃ παρρησίᾳ ὡς πάντοτε καὶ νῦν μεγαλυνθήσεται Χριστὸς ἐν τῷ σώματί μου εἴτε διὰ ζωῆς εἴτε διὰ θανάτου

passages.text: For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul lives for Christ.
Christ gives meaning to Paul's life.
If Paul dies, he gains something better.
Death brings gain for Paul because of Christ.
passages.original: Ἐμοὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῆν Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κέρδος

passages.text: But if I go on living in the body, this will mean fruitful labor for me. So what shall I choose? I do not know.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul is a Christian apostle.
\r\nIf I continue to live in this body, I will have fruitful work.
\r\nI do not know what I should choose.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ ζῆν ἐν σαρκί τοῦτό μοι καρπὸς ἔργου καὶ τί αἱρήσομαι οὐ γνωρίζω

passages.text: I am torn between the two. I desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better indeed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul is a Christian apostle.
\r\nPaul feels torn between two choices.
\r\nPaul desires to depart from this life.
\r\nPaul desires to be with Christ.
\r\nBeing with Christ is far better.
passages.original: συνέχομαι δὲ ἐκ τῶν δύο τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχων εἰς τὸ ἀναλῦσαι καὶ σὺν Χριστῷ εἶναι πολλῷ γὰρ μᾶλλον κρεῖσσον

passages.text: But it is more necessary for you that I remain in the body.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nIt is more necessary for you that I remain in the body.
\r\nMy continued life helps you.
passages.original: τὸ δὲ ἐπιμένειν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἀναγκαιότερον δι’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and will continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith, so that through my coming to you again your exultation in Christ Jesus will resound on account of me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is convinced.
Paul knows he will remain alive.
Paul knows he will stay with all the believers.
Paul will stay for their progress in the faith.
Paul will stay for their joy in the faith.
Paul will come to them again.
When Paul comes, their exultation in Christ Jesus will increase.
Their exultation will be because of Paul’s presence with them.
passages.original: Καὶ τοῦτο πεποιθὼς οἶδα ὅτι μενῶ καὶ παραμενῶ πᾶσιν ὑμῖν εἰς τὴν ὑμῶν προκοπὴν καὶ χαρὰν τῆς πίστεως ἵνα τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν περισσεύῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐμῆς παρουσίας πάλιν πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you in my absence, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, contending side by side for the faith of the gospel, without being frightened in any way by those who oppose you. This is a clear sign of their destruction but of your salvation, and it is from God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
Paul urges them to live in a way that honors the gospel of Christ.
He tells them to conduct themselves in a manner worthy of the gospel.
Paul says this is important at all times.
He says it is important whether he visits them or is absent.
Paul wants to hear good things about them.
He wants to know they stand firm in one spirit.
He wants them to work together with one mind.
He wants them to strive side by side for the faith of the gospel.
Paul tells them not to be afraid of those who oppose them.
He says their courage is a sign.
It is a sign of destruction for their opponents.
It is a sign of salvation for the believers.
This sign comes from God.
passages.original: Μόνον ἀξίως τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολιτεύεσθε ἵνα εἴτε ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ὑμᾶς εἴτε ἀπὼν ἀκούω τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν ὅτι στήκετε ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι μιᾷ ψυχῇ συναθλοῦντες τῇ πίστει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ μὴ πτυρόμενοι ἐν μηδενὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων ἥτις ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς ἔνδειξις ἀπωλείας ὑμῶν δὲ σωτηρίας καὶ τοῦτο ἀπὸ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him, since you are encountering the same struggle you saw I had, and now hear that I still have.
passages.sermon:
God has given you a gift for Christ’s sake.
This gift is not only to believe in Christ.
God has also given you the gift to suffer for Christ.
You are facing the same struggle I faced.
You saw my struggle before.
Now you hear that I still have this struggle.
passages.original: ὅτι ὑμῖν ἐχαρίσθη τὸ ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὐ μόνον τὸ εἰς αὐτὸν πιστεύειν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πάσχειν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀγῶνα ἔχοντες οἷον εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ νῦν ἀκούετε ἐν ἐμοί
